newsitem.title: DENMARK: Carlsberg H1 disappoints Danish market.
newsitem.headline: Carlsberg H1 disappoints Danish market.

text.p: Danish dealers and analysts contacted by Reuters on Tuesday expressed disappointment about Carlsberg's 1996/97 first-half result and predicted modest falls in the brewery's shares.
"Carlsberg's interim operating profit is somewhat disappointing. The pre-tax result was saved by financial items, the share looks like falling moderately on the result," one dealer said.
At 1030 GMT the share traded at 395 crowns, unchanged from Monday's close, but dealers saw it falling to 390 by the end of the day.
An analyst, who asked not to be named, said that the operating result had been hurt by poor growth in China, where the brewery has heavy investment programmes.

"China is costing Carlsberg a lot of money and this is dragging its performance in Asia down. This affects operating results initially, although in the longer term the investment in China should prove sensible," he said.
Carlsberg on Tuesday announced first half pre-tax profit of 870 million crowns, up 17.4 per cent from the same period a year earlier. Turnover rose to 9.21 billion crowns from 8.54 billion.
Analysts had on average forecast pre-tax profit of 812 million crowns and turnover of 8.99 billion.
